html:
Another spelling on the map for Haripunjaya, the Mon kingdom of Lamphun in northern Thailand, shown here in 1200, in its last century. By then its lands reached across the Ping and Wang valleys.

These were its best years as a Buddhist centre. Tradition dates the first form of its great shrine, Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, to the 11th or early 12th century, and its monks kept ties with the Mon of Lower Burma (the Mon states). Its neighbours were changing fast: the Khmer held Lavo to the south, and Tai chiefs were founding new states such as Sukhothai.

In 1292 the Tai king Mangrai took Lamphun after a long siege. Its lands became the heart of Lan Na, and its Mon Buddhist culture passed into the new kingdom.
